2024 
 The Honourable Sri Justice E. V. Venugopal
 Criminal Petition No.2821 Of 2018
O R D E R:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioner, who is arrayed as accused No.15, seeking to quash the proceedings initiated against him in Crime No.665 of 2017 on the file of Chaitanyapuri Police Station, Ranga Reddy District, registered for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 420, 406, 506 r/w 34 of IPC.

entities.text: Chaitanyapuri Police Station, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner/A15 and Ms. S. Madhavi, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.
Perused the record.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the de-facto complainant lodged a complaint dated 13.11.2017 stating that A1 and A2 lured the de-facto complainant and others in the name of providing jobs and business opportunities by collecting huge amount in Crores of rupees by offering high rate of interest.
However, they did not provide any EVV,J employment and also stopped payment of interest.

When the complainant and others approached them for repayment of their amount, they threatened the complainant and others with dire consequences and absconded, thereby, the accused have cheated the de-facto and others.
Basing on the complaint of the de-facto complainant a case was registered against the accused in Crime No.665 of 2017 on the file of Chaitanyapuri Police Station.
During the course of investigation, the name of the petitioner is also figured as accused No.15 in the remand application.
Aggrieved by the same the petitioner/A15 has filed the present Criminal Petition seeking to quash the proceedings initiated against him in Cr.No.665 of 2017.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner appearing online vehemently contended that there is no whisper about involvement of the petitioner in the complaint made by the de-facto complainant,
however, without verifying the facts, the respondent-police mechanically arrayed the petitioner as Accused No.15 in the remand application, basing on the EVV,J alleged confession statement made by accused No.1.

He further contended that the petitioner is an employee of Police Department and was suspended while working as Sub-Inspector of Police and due to political and ulterior motive, a false case has been registered against the petitioner to harass him.
Hence, he prays to allow the Criminal Petition.

5. On the other hand, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the Criminal Petition and the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and contended that unless and until a full-fledged trial is conducted, the truth and involvement of the petitioner in the alleged offence will not come out.
He, therefore, prays to dismiss the Criminal Petition.

sentences.text: However, the petitioner shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer as and when required by furnishing information and documents as sought by him in concluding the investigation.

The petitioner/accused No.15 shall file all the relevant documents in order to prove that the alleged transaction does not come under the criminal offences and on filing such documents, the Investigating Officer shall consider the same before filing appropriate report before the Magistrate concerned.
7. Accordingly, this Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall also stand closed.

He, therefore, prays to dismiss the Criminal Petition.
Without going into the merits of the case, since the punishment prescribed for the offence alleged against the petitioner is less than seven (07) years, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the petitioner/accused to appear before the Investigating Officer on or before 05.09.2024 between 02:00 p.m. and 04:00 p.m. and in turn the EVV,J Investigating Officer is directed to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. and also the guidelines formulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and another 1 scrupulously.
However, the petitioner shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer as and when required by furnishing information and documents as sought by him in concluding the investigation.
The petitioner/accused No.15 shall file all the relevant documents in order to prove that the alleged transaction does not come under the criminal offences and on filing such documents, the Investigating Officer shall consider the same before filing appropriate report before the Magistrate concerned.
7. Accordingly, this Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall also stand closed.
